newsitem.title: GERMANY: Steadier Bremen cotton prices reflect tightness.
newsitem.headline: Steadier Bremen cotton prices reflect tightness.

text.p: Lack of cotton at origin has lifted prices in the Bremen market, where consumers are looking for material, a fortnightly market report from the Bremen Cotton Exchange said.
Yarn spinners were looking to cover supply gaps ahead of the arrival of 1997/98 crops, taking up trade offers when origins were sold out, it said.
New crop business was limited by the firm prices and a strong dollar versus the mark.
Spot trades included Central Asian, U.S. and Indian medium grades.
Reported transactions for 1997 dates included Syrian and Sudanese cotton while West Africans featured in 1998 deals alongside Central Asian and Chadian cotton.
First half 1998 deals involving U.S. and Israel-Pima grades were reported in the extra-longstaple sector.
Cotton stocks as of July 4 totalled 46,173 bales, down from 103,810 bales a year earlier and compared with 43,018 bales a fortnight earlier.
